_note: AI-drafted Call to Worship — pending Wilson's curation.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Go from the land you know to a land you have not seen.
We lift our eyes to the hills; our help comes from the Lord.
The wind blows where it will; so the Spirit moves.
We must be born from above.
For God so loved the world that he gave his only Son.
We will not perish; we have life that does not end.
The Lord keeps your going out and coming in; come, let us worship.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Like Abram, we are pulled from the door of home toward a country over the horizon, with only a promise for a map.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
Lift your eyes to the hills; the One who keeps you does not slumber, does not sleep, walks every mile at your side.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
Come by night if you must, like the man with his questions; the wind is already moving, and you must be born from above.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
For God so loved this world that he gave his only Son, not to condemn the road but to carry us home on it.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
Your going out and your coming in are kept from this time on. Come, let us worship.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross. Keep us, Lord. Amen.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: We set out like Abram, called toward a land unseen.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
We lift our eyes to the hills; our keeper never sleeps.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
Born of the Spirit, loved by the God who gave his Son.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
The Lord keeps our going out and coming in. Come, let us worship.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross. Amen.
